title: The Laptop in the Post
intro: A company you just joined says your laptop is on its way. Experience has made you wary.
But some messages are real. Mirage loves it when you stop trusting the honest ones.

p.text: Track it using the courier number in your Quillon HR portal.
There is nothing to pay. We cover all equipment.

foot.text: Questions? Call your manager or HR on the numbers in your offer letter.

addr.label: The company's real address
addr.lens: It comes from the company's own domain.
addr.why: A matching domain is good evidence.

laptop.label: A laptop the company sends
laptop.lens: The company pays for and sends your equipment.

track.label: Tracked in the portal
track.lens: You check delivery in your own HR portal.
track.why: Pointing you to your own account is honest.

nopay.label: Nothing to pay
nopay.lens: It says the company covers all equipment.
nopay.why: Honest employers never ask you to pay.

hr.label: Real numbers from your offer letter
hr.lens: It points to numbers you already hold.
hr.why: Using contact details you already have is honest.

actions.label: Track the laptop in the HR portal and wait for it

go_ahead.line: The portal showed the courier's number. The laptop arrived on Thursday, and nobody asked for money.

ignore.line: Nothing bad happened. But checking the portal would have told you when to expect it.

block_report.line: That was a real message from your new employer. When every message looks like a scam, real ones get lost too.
block_report.mirageSays: If you trust nothing, I win anyway.

what_if.block_report: The company sent the laptop, asked for nothing, and pointed you to your own HR portal. That is how an honest employer looks.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring was safe. Recognising a real message is the skill: it asks for nothing secret and matches something you know.

golden_rule: An honest employer sends your equipment and never asks you to pay. Check in your own HR portal.

quick_check.q: What made this laptop email honest?

options.text: It had a laptop in it
The company paid for it, asked for nothing and sent you to your own portal

quick_check.explain: Who pays and where you check are the real signs.

hints.nudge: What is this message actually asking you to do?

rows.k: Do honest employers charge for equipment?

rows.v: Use the portal and numbers you already hold
